doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Cooper joins Ellington; the bus wreck and the record date
summary: Cooper recounts meeting the band in Paris, being called for gigs, and the head-on crash on his first night, followed by a recording date.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well one thing I can say about Duke I mean he was not a disciplinarian. By no means. He’d say, “Everybody’s a man.” Or he didn’t fire you, and I mean well he gave one guy notice, that was the first time I’d ever seen that. But anyway, okay now what happened to me, I had met him when I was like in Paris you know. I had the group behind the Josephine Baker show, you know, my brother and I, and the old Olympia Theater like in Paris. So and the band was like in town so they came by the see the group. And they just kind of hit on me then, you know, for coming with the band. And so when I got back to New York I was playing night clubs around New York, right, Count Basie’s Club and Small’s Paradise, in my group. So he called me one time, for a couple of gigs, but I
couldn’t make them. So he called me up for one weekend, you know to make Friday, Saturday, Sunday, over in Cherry Hill, New Jersey you know.
Yes. Exactly. So that’s where it starts. So my first night, no my third night, I—
His first night was Upstate New York somewhere.
That’s right. That’s right. We had a wreck.
We had a head-on collision Buster’s first night.
Betty got hurt, and the bus driver.
And it’s like what happened, okay, he was on the edge of the cliff, you know—
And okay now we had to get a school bus, you know, one of the school buses, to go into New York City, and we had to record that morning.

And we were standing out on the highway for hours, and finally an old rickety school bus comes and picks us up, and drives us straight to the record studio. It doesn’t matter that we had a wreck or anything like that, we’d go to the record date and make the record.
